content:
{
  "findings": [
    {
      "title": "Primary endpoint ORR may not capture clinical benefit in post-platinum cervical cancer",
      "quote": "The primary objective of the study is to estimate the clinical benefit of cemiplimab + ISA101b after progression on first line chemotherapy, as assessed by objective response rate (ORR).",
      "page": 29,
      "section": "2.1 Primary Objective",
      "category": "advisory",
      "severity": "advisory",
      "explanation": "ORR is a surrogate endpoint; in a post-platinum cervical cancer population where immunotherapies may provide disease control without high response rates, ORR may not fully capture clinical benefit. Consider co-primary endpoints like PFS or OS.",
      "fix": "Consider adding PFS or OS as co-primary endpoints or as key secondary endpoints to better capture clinical benefit."
    },
    {
      "title": "Inclusion criterion for prior platinum therapy may be ambiguous",
      "quote": "NOTE: Platinum-therapy given in other settings (eg, concurrent with radiation therapy as part of curative-intent therapy, after radiation [or chemoradiation] as adjuvant treatment in a patient with no evidence of disease) does not satisfy the eligibility requirement regarding prior platinum therapy.",
      "page": 40,
      "section": "7.2.1 Inclusion Criteria",
      "category": "amendment_risk",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "The note clarifies that platinum given in curative/adjuvant settings does not count, but it may be unclear whether patients who received platinum as part of initial treatment and later progressed (without a separate platinum line for metastatic disease) are eligible. This ambiguity could lead to enrollment of patients who do not meet the intended prior platinum requirement.",
      "fix": "Clarify that patients must have received platinum for recurrent/metastatic disease and progressed, or specify that prior platinum in any setting is acceptable if progression occurred after completion."
    },
    {
      "title": "Inclusion criterion for prior bevacizumab is overly complex and may be restrictive",
      "quote": "Patients must meet at least 1 of the following criteria regarding prior bevacizumab therapy: a. Received prior bevacizumab-containing therapy and experienced subsequent progression of disease b. Received prior bevacizumab-containing therapy which was discontinued due to toxicity c. Was unsuitable for bevacizumab due to i) unacceptable risk of fistula formation, ii) poorly controlled hypertension, iii) low risk disease according to Moore criteria d. Refused prior bevacizumab e. Did not have access to bevacizumab",
      "page": 40,
      "section": "7.2.1 Inclusion Criteria",
      "category": "burden",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "The multiple sub-criteria for prior bevacizumab are complex and may be difficult to document, especially 'low risk disease according to Moore criteria' and 'refused prior bevacizumab' which are subjective. This could lead to enrollment delays and potential inconsistencies across sites.",
      "fix": "Simplify the bevacizumab requirement, e.g., allow any prior bevacizumab or documented contraindication, and provide clear definitions for Moore criteria."
    },
    {
      "title": "Inclusion criterion for prior taxol therapy is similarly complex",
      "quote": "Patients must meet at least 1 of the following criteria regarding prior taxol therapy a. Received prior taxol-containing therapy and experienced subsequent progression of disease b. Received prior taxol-containing therapy which was discontinued due to toxicity c. Was unsuitable for taxol therapy due to i) neuropathy, ii) allergy or intolerance to taxol or one of its components d. Refused prior taxol",
      "page": 40,
      "section": "7.2.1 Inclusion Criteria",
      "category": "burden",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "Similar to bevacizumab, the taxol criteria are complex and include subjective elements like 'refused prior taxol' and 'unsuitable due to neuropathy' without specifying severity. This may lead to inconsistent application and potential amendments.",
      "fix": "Simplify the taxol requirement, e.g., allow any prior taxol or documented contraindication, and define neuropathy severity."
    },
    {
      "title": "Exclusion criterion for prior immune-modulating agents may be overly broad",
      "quote": "Prior treatment with other systemic immune-modulating agents that was a. less than 4 weeks (28 days) of the enrollment date, or b. associated with imAEs of any grade within 90 days prior to enrollment, or c. associated with toxicity that resulted in discontinuation of the immune-modulating agent.",
      "page": 41,
      "section": "7.2.2 Exclusion Criteria",
      "category": "amendment_risk",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "The exclusion of patients with any imAE of any grade within 90 days is very broad; even grade 1 imAEs that resolved would exclude a patient. This could unnecessarily limit enrollment and may not be justified for safety.",
      "fix": "Consider excluding only patients with imAEs that required systemic immunosuppression or that did not resolve to grade ≤1."
    },
    {
      "title": "Exclusion criterion for autoimmune disease within 5 years may be too restrictive",
      "quote": "Has ongoing or recent (within 5 years) evidence of significant autoimmune disease that required treatment with systemic immunosuppressive treatments.",
      "page": 41,
      "section": "7.2.2 Exclusion Criteria",
      "category": "amendment_risk",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "The 5-year lookback for autoimmune disease is long and may exclude patients who have been in remission and off immunosuppression for years. This could reduce enrollment and is not standard for checkpoint inhibitor trials, which typically use a shorter window or require active treatment.",
      "fix": "Shorten the lookback period (e.g., 2 years) or specify that only patients requiring ongoing immunosuppression are excluded."
    },
    {
      "title": "Safety monitoring for HPV vaccine (ISA101b) is not specified",
      "quote": "To characterize the safety profile of cemiplimab + ISA101b",
      "page": 29,
      "section": "2.2 Secondary Objectives",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "The protocol does not describe specific safety monitoring for ISA101b, a therapeutic HPV vaccine. Vaccine-related adverse events (e.g., injection site reactions, systemic flu-like symptoms) and potential immune-related events should be explicitly monitored and reported.",
      "fix": "Add a section detailing safety monitoring for ISA101b, including injection site reactions, hypersensitivity, and vaccine-related systemic symptoms."
    },
    {
      "title": "No stopping rules or dose modification guidelines for immune-related adverse events",
      "quote": "Incidence and severity of TEAEs/adverse events of special interest (AESIs)/serious adverse events (SAEs) and ≥ grade 3 laboratory abnormalities during the treatment period and up to 90 days after the last dose of study treatment",
      "page": 35,
      "section": "4.2 Secondary Endpoints",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "critical",
      "explanation": "The protocol lists safety endpoints but does not include explicit stopping rules or dose modification guidelines for immune-related adverse events (irAEs) associated with cemiplimab. This is a critical safety monitoring gap for a checkpoint inhibitor.",
      "fix": "Include a detailed section on management of irAEs, including dose holds, corticosteroid use, and permanent discontinuation criteria."
    }
  ]
}
